question: What is the correct sequence of the nursing process?
options: A. Assessment, Planning, Diagnosis, Implementation, Evaluation
B. Assessment, Diagnosis, Planning, Implementation, Evaluation
C. Diagnosis, Assessment, Planning, Implementation, Evaluation
D. Planning, Assessment, Diagnosis, Implementation, Evaluation
explanation:
• The correct sequence is ADPIE: Assessment, Diagnosis, Planning, Implementation, Evaluation.
• This systematic approach ensures comprehensive patient care.

question: What is the minimum time for effective hand hygiene using alcohol-based hand rub?
explanation:
• WHO recommends 20-30 seconds of rubbing until hands are dry.
• Critical for infection control in RRB syllabus.

question: Which vital sign should be assessed first in an emergency?
explanation:
• ABC approach: Airway, Breathing, Circulation. Respiratory rate reflects breathing.
• In emergency, airway and breathing take priority.

question: What is the correct angle for intramuscular injection in the deltoid?
explanation:
• IM injections are given at 90 degrees to ensure medication reaches muscle.
• Prevents injection into subcutaneous tissue.

question: Which position is best for a patient with dyspnea?
explanation:
• High Fowler's (90°) maximizes lung expansion and reduces diaphragm pressure.
• Improves breathing in respiratory distress.

question: Normal adult blood pressure range (mmHg) is:
explanation:
• Normal adult BP is typically 90/60 to 120/80 mmHg.
• Above 120/80 is elevated; above 130/80 may indicate hypertension.

question: Which isolation is required for tuberculosis?
explanation:
• TB is spread by airborne droplet nuclei; airborne isolation (negative pressure, N95) is required.
• Droplet is for larger particles (e.g. influenza).

question: Yellow bag in BMW management is used for:
explanation:
• Yellow bag: infectious waste, anatomical waste, soiled dressings (BMW Rules 2016).
• Red: recyclable contaminated; White/translucent: sharps.

question: Normal adult respiratory rate per minute is:
explanation:
• Normal adult respiratory rate is 12-20 breaths/minute.
• Tachypnea >20; bradypnea <12.

question: Sterilization in autoclave is achieved by:
explanation:
• Autoclave uses saturated steam at 121°C (15 psi) or 134°C for specified time.
• Most effective for heat-stable instruments.

question: WHO '5 Moments for Hand Hygiene' include:
options: B. Before and after patient contact, before aseptic task, after body fluid exposure, after patient surroundings
explanation:
• 5 moments: before patient contact; before aseptic task; after body fluid exposure; after patient contact; after patient surroundings.
• RRB syllabus emphasizes infection control.

question: Subcutaneous injection is typically given at:
explanation:
• Subcutaneous: 45-90° depending on needle length; pinch skin, inject.
• Common sites: abdomen, thigh, upper arm.

question: Ventrogluteal site for IM injection is preferred because:
options: A. It is the most painful
B. It has minimal nerves and blood vessels, good muscle mass
C. It is the easiest to locate
explanation:
• Ventrogluteal: safe, minimal risk of hitting sciatic nerve or major vessels.
• Preferred over dorsogluteal.

question: Normal adult pulse range per minute is:
explanation:
• Normal adult pulse 60-100/min. Bradycardia <60; tachycardia >100.
• Assess rhythm, strength, equality.

question: Red bag in BMW (Biomedical Waste) is for:
options: B. Contaminated recyclable waste (e.g. tubing, bottles)
explanation:
• Red: contaminated recyclable (plastic, rubber). Yellow: infectious/anatomical. White: sharps.
• BMW Rules 2016.

question: Fowler's position is used for:
options: B. Patients with breathing difficulty, feeding, drainage
explanation:
• Fowler's (semi-sitting) improves breathing, eating, drainage. High Fowler's 90°.
• Common in respiratory and post-op care.

question: First step in nursing process is:
explanation:
• Assessment: collect data (subjective and objective). First step of ADPIE.
• Basis for diagnosis and plan.

question: Disinfection differs from sterilization in that:
options: A. Disinfection kills all microbes including spores
B. Disinfection destroys most pathogens but not necessarily spores
C. Sterilization is only for instruments
explanation:
• Sterilization: destroys all microbes including spores. Disinfection: reduces pathogens, may not kill spores.
• High-level, mid-level, low-level disinfection.

question: Trendelenburg position is contraindicated in:
options: B. Increased intracranial pressure, head injury
explanation:
• Trendelenburg (head down) increases ICP; avoid in head injury, cerebral edema.
• Used cautiously for hypotension.

question: Normal body temperature in Celsius is:
explanation:
• Normal core ~37°C (98.6°F). Fever >38°C. Hypothermia <35°C.
• Vital sign assessment.

question: Standard precautions include:
options: B. Hand hygiene, PPE, safe handling of sharps and body fluids, respiratory hygiene
C. Only for known infected patients
explanation:
• Standard precautions: hand hygiene, gloves, gown, mask/eye protection, sharps safety, environmental control.
• Applied to all patients.

question: Size of Foley catheter commonly used for adult female:
explanation:
• Adult female commonly 14-16 Fr. Adult male 16-18 Fr. Pediatric smaller.
• RRB often asks procedure-related facts.

question: Sims position is used for:
options: B. Rectal examination, enema, perineal care
explanation:
• Sims (left lateral with upper leg flexed): rectal exam, enema, perineal care.
• Promotes drainage and access.

question: Evaluation in nursing process involves:
options: B. Comparing outcomes with goals, determining effectiveness, revising plan if needed
explanation:
• Evaluation: did interventions achieve goals? Revise plan if not.
• Continuous throughout care.

question: Needle stick injury: immediate action is:
options: B. Wash with soap and water, encourage bleeding, report, follow protocol
explanation:
• Wash site with soap and water; encourage bleeding; report; baseline and follow-up testing per protocol.
• Post-exposure prophylaxis as indicated.

question: White/translucent puncture-proof container in BMW is for:
explanation:
• White/translucent: sharps (needles, syringes, blades). Must be puncture-proof.
• Never recap needles; dispose immediately.

question: Knee-chest position is used for:
explanation:
• Knee-chest: rectum and sigmoid access. Patient on knees, chest down.
• Alternative: left lateral.

question: Nursing diagnosis is formulated from:
options: B. Assessment data and clinical judgment
explanation:
• Nursing diagnosis: clinical judgment from assessment (NANDA format).
• Identifies patient problems nurses can treat.

question: Autoclave temperature and time for wrapped instruments (standard):
explanation:
• Standard: 121°C (250°F), 15 psi, 15-30 min for wrapped items.
• Flash: 134°C for 3-4 min unwrapped.

question: Droplet precautions are used for:
options: B. Measles, influenza, pertussis (large droplet spread)
explanation:
• Droplet: particles >5 µm; spread by cough/sneeze. Mask, private room.
• Airborne: smaller particles (TB, measles).

question: Documentation in nursing should be:
options: B. Accurate, timely, factual, complete, legible
explanation:
• Documentation: accurate, timely, factual, complete, legible. Legal record.
• If not documented, not done.

question: Normal oxygen saturation (SpO2) range is:
explanation:
• Normal SpO2 95-100%. <90% may need oxygen. Critical <88%.
• Fifth vital sign in many settings.

question: Informed consent is:
options: B. Patient's voluntary agreement after understanding risks, benefits, alternatives
explanation:
• Informed consent: patient (or surrogate) understands and agrees voluntarily.
• Nurse may witness; provider obtains.

question: Lateral (side-lying) position helps in:
options: B. Preventing pressure ulcers, drainage, airway (unconscious), pregnancy
explanation:
• Lateral: pressure relief, drainage, pregnant women (left lateral), airway in unconscious.
• Alternate sides for pressure ulcer prevention.

question: Implementation in nursing process is:
options: B. Carrying out the planned interventions
explanation:
• Implementation: doing the planned nursing interventions.
• Document as done; reassess as needed.

question: Contact precautions are for:
options: B. MRSA, VRE, C. difficile (direct/indirect contact)
explanation:
• Contact: MRSA, VRE, C. diff, RSV. Gown and gloves; dedicated equipment.
• Prevents spread by touch.

question: Bed making: closed bed is:
options: A. Bed with patient in it
B. Unoccupied bed with top linen folded back
explanation:
• Closed bed: unoccupied, linens in place. Open bed: top linens fan-folded for patient.
• Occupied bed: made with patient in bed.

question: Hypothermia is core temperature below:
explanation:
• Hypothermia: core <35°C. Mild 32-35°C; moderate 28-32°C; severe <28°C.
• Rewarm gradually; monitor.

question: Nurse's role in consent:
options: B. Witness signature, ensure patient understood; provider explains and obtains
explanation:
• Nurse may witness consent; ensure patient is competent and not coerced.
• Physician/provider explains procedure and obtains consent.

question: Disinfection with 0.5% sodium hypochlorite is used for:
explanation:
• Bleach (sodium hypochlorite) for surface disinfection, blood spills.
• Correct concentration and contact time required.
